summary: Loang Him Kao (‘Blue Street’) in San Klang, east of Chiang Mai, is a community of independent craft makers whose homes and studios open as small shops. Browse locally designed textiles and indigo-dyed clothes and accessories, then add the weekend Chamcha Market for more maker stalls, food and coffee. This is primarily a retail and browsing outing: artisan workshops are occasional or require advance arrangement, so do not assume a walk-in class.
whyGo: See craft makers’ own studios and shops in a community built around local art, craft and self-sufficiency.
Indigo textiles are a local specialty; named shops include Slow Stitch and Anda Indigo, alongside broader craft stalls.
The shaded weekend market adds independent makers, food and a relaxed setting under large rain trees.
bestFor: Textile and craft enthusiasts who prefer independent studios and small makers to a conventional mall.
A half-day outing that can include browsing, lunch or coffee and the nearby Bo Sang craft area.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed dye workshop, fixed class price or confirmed artisan demonstration without arranging it ahead.
You cannot visit on a weekend and need several stalls to be open together; individual studios have separate schedules.
duration: Allow 2–3 hours for the community and Chamcha Market, plus travel. This is a planning estimate; time depends on which studios are open and whether you stop for food.
cost: No admission charge is published for browsing the community or market. Purchases and food are extra; workshop prices are not published and must be confirmed with the individual maker.
hours: A current local listing describes Chamcha Market as open Saturday and Sunday, 09:00–15:00. Loang Him Kao’s studios are independent: a 2025 local feature says the lane can be visited daily, 09:00–17:00, but shop opening varies. Check the market’s current social page and contact any specific studio before travelling.
bestTime: Arrive in the morning, especially for the weekend market. December is outside the usual September–November indigo harvest workshop season cited by Studio Naenna; general retail browsing remains the more reliable plan.
gettingThere: Loang Him Kao is in Ban Mon, San Klang, San Kamphaeng, roughly 15 km east of central Chiang Mai according to a local community profile. A taxi or ride-hail/private driver is the practical option; arrange a return ride if relying on a driver. There is parking at the market according to a local guide. Public transport details were not verified.
booking: No booking is needed for ordinary market browsing. Contact a particular shop before visiting if you want to meet a maker or see a working studio. For actual dyeing, Studio Naenna lists private group tie-dye and half/full-day visits by arrangement, with advance booking required; its three-day indigo harvest workshops are normally September–November, subject to plant and date availability. Email st.naenna@gmail.com or call +66 53 226 042 to ask about December options and current fees. Studio Naenna is a separate venue in Chang Phueak, not in Loang Him Kao.
accessibility: The market is outdoors under trees, and the source describes plentiful parking, but step-free paths, accessible toilets, seating and studio access are not documented. Expect open-air lanes and ask the venue about surfaces and facilities if access needs matter.
practicalTips: Treat maker shops as separate businesses; check opening status before making a special trip on a weekday.
Ask whether textiles are made or dyed by the vendor, what fibres and dye process are used, and whether prices are fixed.
Keep a workshop and a browsing visit distinct in your plan: a market stall does not establish that a class is running.
The NAP Fair is listed by Studio Naenna for 5–11 December 2026 on Nimmanhaemin Soi 1; it is a separate Chiang Mai makers’ fair, not an event at Loang Him Kao.
decemberNotes: The 2026 NAP Fair is dated 5–11 December at Nimmanhaemin Soi 1, according to Studio Naenna’s activity page, offering a city-centre alternative for browsing local makers. No special Loang Him Kao December programme or 2026 holiday opening schedule was verified. Confirm Chamcha Market and individual studio hours shortly before the intended weekend. Studio Naenna says its plant-to-paste indigo workshop normally takes place September–November, so December availability is not established; arrange and confirm any alternative session directly.
uncertainties: No published admission, workshop prices, market stall roster or guaranteed demonstration schedule was found.
Opening times vary between sources and among independent shops; the current local market listing gives 09:00–15:00 weekends, while an older magazine listing gives earlier hours.
No specific accessibility information or confirmed December 2026 workshop dates at Loang Him Kao were available.
